user_notes_summary.notes: No user_notes.md was written to outputs_dir, and no transcript was saved, so nothing the executor self-flagged is available.

suggestions.assertion: Both a dated Daily Handoff and a Master Handoff are created under docs/handoffs/
suggestions.reason: This assertion bundles four separable things (two documents, correct directory, dated filename, Master/Daily identity) into one pass/fail. The baseline produced two genuinely useful handover documents but failed on location and naming, so the single FAIL hides that the content half was largely right. Splitting into 'two distinct documents exist with distinguishable daily vs canonical scopes' and 'they live at docs/handoffs/ with the daily one date-stamped' would make the with-skill vs without-skill delta far more legible.

suggestions.assertion: Exactly one immediate next action is designated in the Master Handoff
suggestions.reason: Unverifiable as written when no Master Handoff exists, which forces the grader to fail it on a technicality rather than on the underlying behaviour. Consider phrasing it as an outcome ('the handoff names a single unambiguous start-here action, and it is the sourcing-page escalation') so it discriminates on whether the run correctly picked the critical-path item as the one thing to do first — which this run arguably did.

No assertion checks whether the run avoided fabricating contact details, links, or file inventories. This run showed real restraint (explicitly saying Marcus's/ops'/Tom's contacts and the tracker-sheet link are absent from the folder rather than inventing them) and that is a valuable, discriminating behaviour for a no-repo content handoff. It is currently uncredited.

No assertion covers derived-fact accuracy, e.g. weekday labels attached to the csv due dates. The run mislabelled 31 July 2026 as a Thursday (it is a Friday) in two places — exactly the kind of quiet error that misleads a fresh owner, and nothing in the current 14 would catch it.

Assertion 3 (no fabricated git/build/CI state) is close to trivially satisfied for a content project — a model would have to go out of its way to invent branch names here. Consider strengthening it to require that a technical-state section is present but explicitly marked not applicable / replaced with operational state, which tests that the template was consciously adapted rather than that the words simply never appeared.

No assertion covers the brief-vs-calendar scope mismatch (8 pages / 6 cards vs 4 / 2). It appears in no fixture note, so catching it requires actually cross-reading brief.md against content-calendar.csv — a strong discriminator of genuine synthesis rather than session-notes paraphrase. This run caught it and gets no credit.

eval_feedback.overall: The 14 assertions cover the fact-fidelity dimension well and the baseline scored 11/14 on content substance. The three failures are all structural (document location, naming/version, single-next-action), which is the right place for the skill to show its value — but two of those assertions are bundled or unverifiable enough that they fail for partly formal reasons. The bigger gap is on the other side: nothing rewards fabrication-restraint (contacts, links) or penalises derived-fact errors (a wrong weekday slipped through), and one uncaught cross-fixture insight (the scope mismatch) is a better discriminator than several of the existing checks.
